answer: The rule groups identities by their behavioural signature and applies the penalty to the whole group at once. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The terrace is the collateral at risk, the island the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the lantern the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many island groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the terrace into smaller, individually useless stakes.
